messages:
asha: quick heads-up — ran a targeted perf sweep on the prod-rt canary for the last deploy (flashattn + triton + cuBLASLt combos). hitting intermittent OOMs when mix of long chat sessions and KV cache growth align. attaching short profile dump we grabbed.

asha: ```
PROFILE SNAPSHOT
model=redwood-13b-encdec
shapes: batch=3, seq=2048/4096 mix, heads=32, dhead=128
kernel decisions: attn -> flashattn_fwd (seq<=2048) workspace=4.8GB; attn fallback (triton) workspace=2.1GB
ffn -> cublaslt_gemm (preferred) temp=6.1GB; triton_ffn temp=3.0GB
kv_cache reserve grew ~1.2GB during trace
peak approx = 11.3GB + persistent allocations (net ~42.4GB on 48GB card) -> OOM triggered when KV spike hit
stack: slab allocator shows fragmentation: free but unusable ~2.6GB
```

dmitri: ugh. two things stand out: (1) cublaslt for FFN is expensive temp-wise; (2) slab fragmentation + kv spikes. did you run with kvpad enabled? hit rate? :thinking:

asha: kvpad=false for this canary (we're testing raw growth). hit-rate was stable ~92% but background retention TTL allowed some growth. spike correlated with parallel seq=4096 stream starting.

marco: sounds like kernel selector is picking min-latency but not min-working-set. for these shapes we should bias selector by workspace footprint when headroom < threshold. propose quick config:

marco: ```yaml
kernel_selector:
  attn:
    prefer: ["flashattn","triton_fallback"]
    seq_workspace_threshold: 1536  # prefer triton when seq larger than this if headroom low
  ffn:
    prefer: ["triton","cublaslt"]
    workspace_cap_mb: 5120
```

sophia: +1. also allocator-level: if we can allow transient temp buffers (ffn temp / attn temp) to be pooled and reused across kernels we'll avoid duplicated peaks. currently cublaslt allocs happen after flashattn so both live at once. reuse would reduce peak by ~6GB in your numbers.

asha: great point. quick trace shows order: attn alloc -> attn temp -> attn free -> ffn alloc -> ffn temp -> ffn free. but free isn't immediate because slab fragmentation prevents coalescing; small freed chunks not usable for the big ffn temp, so allocator ends up allocating new block.

ash: (typo) asha: I think two-pronged fix: (A) lower workspace cap for cublaslt ffn on 40/48GB GPUs when kvreserve > X; (B) enable cross-kernel transient-pool + proactive defragmentation after attn stage.

ci-bot: perf-ci: ran memprof with --track-allocs on canary #2798, small report: peak=42.1GB, fragmentation=2.4GB, largest_free_block=1.6GB, number_of_free_chunks=187. https://ci/reports/2798/memprof

dmitri: For immediate mitigation we can change batching heuristic to avoid mixing long seq tails into same batch as short ones for this model class. i.e., prefer homogenous seq batches or cap batch tokens when kv cache > 1GB. cheap to flip.

marco: agree. Also consider 'workspace headroom margin' calculation change: currently margin = 5% + 100MB. change to margin = max(5%, kv_growth_pct*token_scale) + 400MB floor. That makes selector prefer smaller-workspace kernels when KV unstable.

asha: I'll open a small PR with: 1) kernel selector bias for FFN (workspace cap 5GB), 2) batcher change to avoid mixed-long batches by default, and 3) enable transient temp pool with a conservative reuse policy (must be same lifetime window).

sophia: run memprof with --force-coalesce after attn to validate fragmentation impact. also add a microbench test that sequences: attn->ffn with artificially low coalescing window to reproduce.

asha: plan: PR today for canary tomorrow morning, will include perf CI traces and memprof logs. if canary looks stable we'll roll to dedicated pools.

marco: marking follow-ups: #1 update selector config, #2 allocator pool + small defrag hook, #3 batcher heuristic tweak, #4 add regression test. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: noted — created perf issue #RINF-5872 with attached memprof link and checklist.

asha: thanks team — will post PR link here when ready.
